source.title: Scaling Recurrence-aware Foundation Models for Clinical Records via Next-Visit Prediction
source.authors: H. Rajamohan; Xiangyu Gao; Weicheng Zhu; Shih-Lun Huang; Long Chen; Gabe Schulman; Hui Jin; Shengduo Li; Yixuan Wang; Hui Yang; Kyunghyun Cho; Cem M. Deniz; Narges Razavian

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary information are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures pretraining loss across model sizes and data budgets in a different modality and training regime, and reports a U-shaped relationship rather than a single power law. It also reports scaling results for downstream forecasting.
record.gate_note: The pretraining-loss scaling sweep and downstream metrics across model sizes and data budgets bear on the claim. The paper cites language-model scaling studies, but cited results are not recorded as rows. No exact pretraining-loss values are stated in text or tables; the relevant curves are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study trains EHR next-visit decoder Transformers from 0.69M to 849M parameters on four data budgets to convergence. It reports pretraining loss and downstream zero-shot AUROC as functions of size and data. That is a new modality and a repeated-epoch regime, with results bearing on V5, V6 and V7. No power law is fitted. Data is deliberately the bottleneck, so V1–V3 are not tested as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that in a data-constrained, compute-saturated regime, EHR loss is U-shaped in model size, and that the optimal size grows with the data budget. They call EHR scaling a capacity–data matching problem. Downstream gains plateau beyond about 144M while more data keeps helping, so they recommend acquiring data over adding parameters. They also note that the regularized objective gives broadly consistent scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses decoder-only Transformer models for structured EHR next-visit prediction, training across finite cohort subsets to validation convergence rather than testing the original language-model parameter/token/compute scaling setup. It does not fit the original power-law form or conduct fixed-compute optimal allocation sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss-size curves and selected model-size minima vary with the data budget; the paper also reports a different curve behavior with recurrence-aware weighting, though regularized results are described as broadly consistent with standard pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: With unlimited compute and repeated epochs, the loss-optimal model size grows with dataset size: about 47M for the 10–50% subsets and about 144M for full data. Larger models overfit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In data-constrained, compute-saturated training, the validation-loss-optimal parameter count rises with the amount of unique data.

record.problems: Pretraining-loss curves are presented as figures without exact loss values or stated confidence intervals. The authors say additional data-budget levels would be needed to trace a strict power law. Experiments use one health-system cohort, limiting evidence about other EHR settings.
record.rows_left_out: Did not include downstream macro-AUPRC rows or task-by-task disease forecasting results; the cataloged downstream scaling rows use macro-AUROC from Tables S9 and S10. Also omitted non-scaling forecasting comparisons in Tables 1–2 and EHRSHOT transfer results because they do not measure the scaling claims.

untested.parts: Not language models, and data is deliberately the bottleneck. There is no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
Compute is unconstrained, and there is no fixed-compute allocation of parameters versus tokens.
Width-to-depth ratio varied across configurations but no shape-specific result is reported.
Image, video, fine-tuning and transfer regimes are not tested. The functional form of EHR loss scaling is not fitted.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter counting conventions, schedules, or exponents across setups.

missing.what: Location of the fitted loss minima per data budget (47M for the 10/25/50% subsets, 144M for full data)
Qualitative statement that pretraining loss correlates largely with downstream performance; no number is given
Macro AUPRC series across size and data budget (declared left out but relevant to V6), e.g. 5y AUPRC 0.093→0.115 at 0.69M→2.81M

record.verdict_notes: The U-shape arises because data is the deliberate bottleneck, so it does not contradict V1 as stated. That is why V5 is limits_scope rather than challenges. The data-budget AUROC series is confounded with a model-size change at 100% (47M→144M). Text and table disagree on several values: full-data AUROC is 0.770 in the text vs 0.780 in Table S10 (2y), and 0.751 vs 0.752 (5y). Per-step AUROC changes mostly fall within the 95% CIs, so the record's reversed and observed states for small steps were downgraded. No loss values are given; all loss rows are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: The models are structured EHR models, not language models; the study does not test the stated language-model power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict losses of much larger runs.
Training is convergence-oriented with unconstrained compute and repeated passes over finite data, not a fixed-compute-budget comparison of optimal parameter and token allocations.
Configurations vary in width-to-depth ratio, but the paper does not report a controlled result isolating architecture-shape effects at fixed parameter count.

Tests EHR next-visit pretraining loss across model size and data budgets in a repeated-epoch, compute-saturated setting; does not test image/video, other modalities, fine-tuning or transfer as pretraining regimes.
Reports zero-shot disease-forecasting AUROC across model sizes and data budgets; does not establish a general predictive law for other downstream tasks or quantify a relationship to pretraining loss.

Reports bending/U-shaped loss curves and notes insufficient data-budget levels to trace a strict power law. It does not compare fitting methods, parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, or estimate how fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations change across setups.

relationships.condition: EHR next-visit pretraining, finite cohort, 10–20 repeated epochs to convergence, standard and regularized objectives
relationships.reason: Loss falls with size only up to a data-dependent optimum, then rises (U-shape). No power-law form is fitted, and the authors say they cannot trace a strict power law (loss-std-* and loss-reg-* rows; Fig. 5).
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreased with model size up to a data-dependent optimum and then increased, preventing the authors from tracing a strict power law.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: EHR next-visit pretraining, finite cohort, 10–20 repeated epochs to convergence, standard and regularized objectives
source_check.reason: The standard loss rows show improvement followed by overfitting, and regularized results are described as broadly consistent. This qualifies monotone power-law extension to this regime. No power-law fit is reported; its absence alone is not evidence against V5.

relationships.reason: Loss-vs-size curves bend into a U-shape instead of following one power law, and the fitted minimum shifts with data budget (loss rows; Fig. 5).
relationships.display_finding: Loss versus model size became U-shaped rather than following a single power law, and the fitted minimum shifted with the data budget.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: The loss rows and Figure 5 report U-shaped size curves whose fitted minima shift with data budget, supporting setup-dependent curvature. These are fixed-data curves, not a compute-optimal frontier.

relationships.condition: Increasing pretraining data budget (10%→100%), and the smallest size step (0.69M→2.81M)
relationships.reason: Macro AUROC rises from 0.755 to 0.780 (2y) and from 0.723 to 0.752 (5y) across data budgets. The size step 0.69M→2.81M gives +0.032 (2y) and +0.042 (5y) (data-auroc-*, size-auroc-281-*).
relationships.display_finding: Macro AUROC increased from 0.755 to 0.780 for two-year predictions and 0.723 to 0.752 for five-year predictions with more data, while the smallest size increase added 0.032 and 0.042, respectively.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Increasing pretraining data budget (10%→100%), and the smallest size step (0.69M→2.81M)
source_check.reason: Tables S9–S10 support the reported endpoint gains: data-budget AUROC 0.755→0.780 and 0.723→0.752; smallest-model AUROC gains 0.032 and 0.042. The data sweep also changes selected capacity from 47M to 144M; no quantitative predictive law is fitted.

relationships.condition: Parameter scaling on full data beyond ~14–47M, and the 25%→50% data step
relationships.reason: AUROC plateaus around 0.775–0.781 (2y) and 0.748–0.755 (5y) from 14–47M up to 849M. Steps are within the CIs, there is a dip at 5.81M, and the 50% data budget is flat (size-auroc-581/14m/47m/144m/446m/849m, data-auroc-50-*).
relationships.display_finding: AUROC stayed around 0.775–0.781 for two-year prediction and 0.748–0.755 for five-year prediction from roughly 14–47M through 849M parameters, with changes within confidence intervals, a dip at 5.81M and no gain from 25% to 50% data.

relation.reason: The study directly varies model capacity and data budget and reports held-out pretraining loss and downstream forecasting performance.

tranche.reason: The central scaling result and explicit argument qualify the usual scaling paradigm: finite-cohort repeated training produces U-shaped loss and requires capacity–data matching. T5 describes this scope correction more specifically than T3.

source_check.notes: The paper inconsistently describes regularized loss as U-shaped while also saying its right tail decreases. Downstream prose also differs from Tables S9–S10; the verdict endpoint numbers agree with those tables.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: RAVEN EHR pretraining; repeated-epoch finite-data training across tested data budgets
reader_labels.reason: Validation and test loss are described as U-shaped with model size, including eventual overfitting, rather than following one power law; the regularized full-data curve still has a U-shaped form (loss rows loss-std-val-10 through loss-reg-test-full).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Increasing data budget; and increases at some parameter-size steps in internal zero-shot disease forecasting
reader_labels.reason: Macro AUROC rises across 10% to full data at the 5-year horizon and at several model-size steps, including the marked 0.69M-to-2.81M increase at 5 years (data-auroc-10-5y through data-auroc-100-5y; size-auroc-069-2y through size-auroc-849m-5y).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Parameter scaling on full data, especially beyond the smaller models; 2-year data-budget series
reader_labels.reason: Downstream AUROC is not uniformly increasing with model size: the 2-year sequence includes decreases and the paper describes plateauing or diminishing performance beyond 144M; 2-year data-budget AUROC also dips at 50% data (size-auroc-581-2y, size-auroc-446m-2y, data-auroc-50-2y).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: EHR scaling with finite cohorts, repeated epochs, and convergence-oriented training
reader_labels.reason: The study reports a U-shaped loss-size relationship and says larger datasets shift the fitted minima toward larger models, while noting it cannot trace a strict power law without more data-budget levels (loss rows loss-std-val-10 through loss-reg-test-full).
